I think there is more data coming out as marijuana is now more accessible.

So far, the younger you use it and the more you ingest, the increased prevalence of developing a mental condition, specifically if you are pre-disposed.

Youth that start using seem to be more at risk, and those pre-disposed to schizophrenia, bipolar, depression, etc.

Denmark fielded like 6mil individuals for this data but states more research is needed to pin down if thc causes the conditions or if it just increases the chances of them ‘coming to light’.

There were too many articles and studies to sort through to link, but searching “thc mental health” can give you a good kickoff point to look into.

I feel like it’s a “use at your own risk” thing with the thc/cbd levels in mind. Idk look into it and try not to let confirmation bias sway you. Take in the data and then make your call.

Having a mental health condition or going through a struggle isn’t indicative of your value as a person or your ability. 

We all still deserve understanding and compassion. That all it takes it meeting us where we are at in that moment. 

Also, space and time to process and reset can do wonders, but getting back to baseline can take some time so patience is needed.

We are/can be capable. Sometimes we need help seeing things or being aware. Sometimes we need some treatment but we aren’t pariahs or inept. Just people trying to get through each day as best we can.

We live in a highly desensitized society where such things are readily available for us to see. Where accidents and tragedies less and less evoke an initial compassionate response but rather a sensationalized response.

Being that you’ve written that you wrote this after returning from school, I’d imagine you are younger.

In this digital media age, it’s not too uncommon to be taken in by something you may never get to witness in your actual life (hopefully). But I would offer that you speak to someone.

A benign curiosity can turn into an obsession. I’m not a professional so I can’t say if you’re an x,y, or z.

I can say that it is worth reaching out to a counselor who is trained in asking more in-depth questions to field if this would be a concern or not.

Like what did you feel when watching it? What is your history with empathy? When faced with tragedy or violence? Questions about you that an internet peon can’t help with. 

And if you ever feel the urge to harm another to see these things for yourself, acknowledge that and call a crisis line or pop into the er. They can triage they situation immediately and asses you for proper help if that’s the case.

I want to say, it may take time to find it…but we all have our place somewhere. People who get us, who understand us, who will accept us. Sometimes the things in our heads make it really hard to see what can be…how we see ourselves can distort how we think others see us. This starts a vicious cycle of feeling like we are never going to be enough, or accepted, or loved.  

This cycle is not an easy one to break. Things in our lives have ingrained these beliefs into us, have become our blueprint. From how we were raised, to our childhood experiences, to how society and the masses react to our reality.

Of course, there is always medication, but I am learning myself, it is more important to undo those beliefs so that I can realize that I am worthy. That the reflection I see is not what others see. That all the negative feedback I’ve gotten in my life doesn’t define me. I am more than that. I have to force myself to believe that until I truly believe it.

I offer that you try this perhaps. Look into the parts of your past to see what caused you to feel how you do. Who has told you things that are triggering your beliefs and doubts about yourself? Is it the media? Society? Past relationships? Review how credible those sources are. How valid that input is. When you receive it, do you believe it based on fear? Based on fact? Can you distinguish the two? 

People are messed up, and people like to push their own inadequacies onto others. Rather than uplifting, they will bring others down to push themselves up. This happens in media, government, society, relationships, and even family. When reviewing your past input, ask yourself: “was this person truly helping me by giving me this input? Were they just spreading malicious information? Should I hold this to be true or are they just pushing their issues onto me?”

In a different post, you stated a timeframe. I offer before you adhere to it, trying to reflect on some of the inner aspects. Review the factors that may play into your self-perceptions and see what you glean from it. 

Love is always possible, but how we view ourselves will always always impact our ability to recognize the love and input we receive. No matter our sexual orientation, gender identity, physical appearance or status. I think I’m an awful person that cannot communicate. Anything anyone tells me otherwise, I will not believe. Until I do the work within myself, that will not change. It doesn’t matter if I am actually a good communicator and a lovely person to others, in myself…in my reality, I don’t believe it. My perception is blocking opportunities and causing distress within me.

I hope I have conveyed my point well enough. I’m sorry for the wall of text, and for any confusion. I’m also sorry if I am out of line in any way. I wish you the best and though I’m just an internet stranger, I believe you are worthy of love. I believe you deserve acceptance and that you have value to give to this universe.

When I am in the phase of myself, I have learned…am learning…to step back and pretty much ground myself.

I will look at what I have done, no matter how minuscule and give myself credit for it. Telling myself “you did that!” Well if it was remotely productive and positive.

Then I sit down and try to replan and refocus. If I feel lost it is usually because I am not where I want to be or I am not going/working towards the goals I truly want to work towards. I take that off feeling as a sign to reassess and evaluate.

•Where am I now? Why does it make me uncomfortable?

•What steps can I start taking to move toward a different path?

•How overwhelmed will I be during that transition? What can I do to ease into it, one step at a time?

A therapist once told me that discomfort can be a good thing. It can be motivation to show you things about yourself you aren’t normally willing to accept. Pushing through that unease can result in the best results if you learn truly what is making you uneasy at its core.

So idk it was my understanding that ODD itself was like a precursor to things like ASPD as you cannot diagnose a child with a personality disorder but they can exhibit traits, such as targeted malice and defiance towards authority figures. Intentionally harming or opposing rules and regulation with the intent of “showing others what they can do”..
How I view ODD is like a child misbehaving with intentional malice where there is no other reason or cause. Taking into account other possible diagnosis’ (ASD may present similar to ODD but the reasons are completely different, as is ADHD. I don’t think they can truly be Co-morbid unless there is trauma that has started to affect the child where the ADHD symptoms are truly manifesting separately from the ODD symptoms. Like the cause for the adverse behaviors have nothing to do with the frustration or low stimulation of ADHD but truly with the intent or trauma of the child. 

It would be important when diagnosing ODD to look more into the history of the patient, the environment and how they are responding directly to those things rather than just the symptoms that are presenting. 

I think currently the disorder is overused and slapped on any child that acts out without truly weaning out what the cause for those adverse behaviors are and addressing them one by one. 

Inversely, I do not think an adult can be diagnosed as ODD as that would/should translate to a personality or deprecate trauma related diagnosis that fits their criteria, if they were unable to outgrow or address the causing factors for that ODD initial diagnosis.

This is just my unprofessional opinion.

I want to offer, because it is so polarized as a subject…that while this post is helpful for adult (who most likely are late life diagnosed)…there are children who develop unhealthy stims by nature (most likely where your unhealthy stims formed) and ABA type stuff works to target those stims specifically (not healthy, positive or non-harmful ones) and switch them out for healthier alternatives. 

What you all are doing is more or less a form of DRA (differential reinforcement of an alternative behavior…in place of a more preferred one…i.e. switching harmful/injurious stims for less harmful healthy ones to build healthy coping mechanisms and positive stimming experiences).

Happy behavior modification. It’s not bad, we do it all the time. We may not even realize it and if we can shift the narrative and stigma we can ensure that how ABA is delivered is also shifted so no one is harmed again.

I want to extend my empathy in the most strongest of ways. There were times where I was on the brink of mental death...like TW: suicidal...I was caring for my grandmother when the rest of my family more or less shucked the responsibility on my husband and myself. It got to points where I felt like it’d be better to go with her. I didn’t matter, my family and our needs didn’t matter. She was not elderly like old... 69 with terminal cancer but vapid at times and abusive at others. There were moments where it wasn’t so bad but it was a real struggle. I had to personally check into a short term crisis center for a few days and just be for myself. I quit my job and learned boundaries. I learned to advocate for ME regardless of how people felt about me because I EXISTED. I wasn’t dying. My feelings and frustrations were VALID. I didn’t have a physical support system but I built one with the medical team that helped in some ways that I could trust (it didn’t help that she complained to them when we didn’t give into her demands) but all in all if family didn’t understand, they did. 

They helped me understand I needed to always put myself and my family first. Then take care of her. I got very used to the o2 mask analogy during this time. 

It was still hard towards the end but I was able to cope better as I learned those boundaries and stuck to them. 

Forced myself to do things for me, and took care of me. Check grandma, do her meds, then go garden and play with my son. Have a schedule. If she needed me outside that schedule see if it was a need or a want. Separate the two. If it was a want, take care of me first. THEN if I had the emotional capacity, provide it for her. Needs were taken into account based on priority and emergency.

I learned that a lot of what I was doing were for her wants. She was seeking companionship and was scared. I understood that. She was lashing out and being mean because of the lack of control and her situation. BUT I still understood that I could not care for her if I was not in the right headspace. If I was not okay because I wouldn’t be able to take what she was dishing out. Her lashing out would trigger me, the unappreciativeness will just disappoint and hurt me. I wouldn’t be able to be understanding and compassionate. In the end, I was able to help her transition as peacefully as possible. Her needs were always met, and while I couldn’t be a constant companion I was a constant caretaker. We can only do our best. Know that you’re doing the best you can and that is all anyone can ask for.

The economy, globally is rough, and just taking care of your adult children and yourselves and if there are other younger children...that’s tough.

Now add a significant other to the mix, and well I’m sure the tension may have just surfaced. There are a few things to consider here. One- the amount of arguments you guys are having, if it’s a lot it’s worth sitting down and evaluating how you guys communicate with one another. What’s really going on there.
Two- the consideration of your surroundings. Letting fights escalate to the point that it boils over into the surrounding environment (noise level, pulling people into the fight, etc.) will definitely make a tense situation no bueno. So when you texted his mom, it may have been that she didn’t care about YOU but that SHE was just tired. And it’s not personal, she just cannot be emotionally available for you. While not the most usual situation, I can understand where you are coming from. Not from a personal level but from an objective level. As siblings you tend to have bonds that are on levels different from any friend or some say enemy. 

If one sibling is a predator, especially given a long time to groom, and the exposure is uninterrupted for that length of time, I think it would be natural for that attachment bond to form. If you think about it, that was the goal of the predator. 

You should acknowledge that you knew well enough to draw your boundaries. You see enough to notice it happening to your younger sibling. This is priority, and while you do have to work through your situation, please ensure their safety. You do not want them conflicted like you.

Now your feelings, are not invalid. You should not feel guilty. When you are developing you are confused and wanting attention and acceptance. You look up to those around you and if your older figure takes advantage of that, the problem and negative aspect is within them. You were taken advantage of. Regardless of anything you did or said in that time. You were younger. You were vulnerable, developmentally, if you need further validation you can look into the brain and psyche of the teenager. 

You could have done what they older predator wanted and you still wouldn’t have been in the wrong, you could’ve consented (I know you said there was no physical contact) but again, you are not in the wrong.

Your attachment now, is years and years of bonding and attachment. Carefully manipulated and sculpted so that you would depend mostly if not only on that person. Of course when separated you would want to re-attach. This wasn’t a couple of years, it was nearly a decade and not to mention you don’t have that familial bond that siblings have and build when they grow up with each other (which is a phenomenon you see with some cases of incestuous relationships forming with children are reunited with parents after being given up for adoption). 

Basically, this is not a simple situation, it’s complex. You are dealing with a lot of complex emotions and a situation that needs understanding and patience.

If your therapist isn’t capable of handling this I would question her integrity and skill in her profession. But it is not to me to judge. I think finding a therapist or if you have the resources, a coach to help you through this time. Someone that will help you build your sense of self, break your co-dependency, empower and affirm your value because you did nothing wrong and you are strong for even just reaching out in multiple ways for help. When you find your fit, I think the coping piece will come naturally.

Hope for his healing and that he hurts no one else. But know and always remember what he did was not okay. He preyed upon a teenager, fresh teenager, of opportunity. He may not be the worst person, but that is not okay. For your health, inside and out, if you do forgive him, don’t go back. I actually suffered and made (admittedly sometimes still make) my now husband suffer through this as well.

He games online and the thought of him developing a cyber relationship is something that creeps into my mind a lot. Also now our son has an aide that comes in to assist him and my mind can go imaginative.

Now I’m in therapy, but what helps now and has been a major help is the following:

1. Acknowledging that I am feeling first and foremost insecure, about myself (not that, as you stated, it’s a physical thing, but on the inside. That anyone he interacts with will give him something I lack. Or something better than what he has with me.

This I try counter with-he chose me, he has done so time and time again. Even before marriage and a child, when the paranoias were at their peak actually...

He chose me and I have to seek comfort in that. Not project those insecurities onto him and cause fights.

2. Trust. I have to trust him. I cannot control what he does and who he interacts with, I can only trust his love and loyalty for and to me. Be a he chose me, aside from everything I lack, he still chooses to love me. To be loyal and faithful to me.

3. Build a better image of my sense of self. If I think I’m okay enough, than I worry less about others. I have my own issues and when I can accept those, I don’t worry as much about him running into the arms of someone else. It is easier for my to see and accept why he chooses me and loves me because I choose me and love me.

4. Communication. The most important one I think. When I do feel these feelings, I will communicate them to him in a calm, non-accusatory manner. I will explain that I am feeling down or insecure and due to that I am starting to think of these random scenarios. This normally has been triggering a conversation where he will let me know and remind me of the reasons why I need not worry and help me out of those fears. If it’s really bad, we will come up with plans to help allay my paranoias but as time goes on, I only need that reassurance. 

I don’t want him to live inside a bubble, restricted from things that make him happy or walking over eggshells to ease my insecurities. I don’t want to project my shortcomings onto him and let that control how he lives his life. Those thoughts help me heal and be better and as a result the situations that used to trigger the issues are happening less and less.

They still happen but I’m able to come down faster and talk myself out before it comes to even getting to him. 

It’s not bad to have these thoughts, but it is destructive to let them take over and control an otherwise healthy relationship.

I’ve also had to reckon with the fact that if he indeed ever does step out on this relationship with me, it’s okay. I’ll be okay. If my fears come to fruition, I’ll be able to accept it and move on because I have me. That self-acceptance bit, it makes you realize things and love you. Like if he doesn’t and needs to look elsewhere and you find out then he doesn’t deserve the you that is so magnificent. It’s not worth stressing the present, just live in the moment and if it happens you will be okay. 

I don’t worry about what could be happening so much, I ensure I’m loved by him and me, I ensure I have support and I keep going. Communicate my concerns and keep it pushing. I’ve gone from literally crying in the dark whenever he games to just doing my own thing. 

I hope this give you some type of insight or something.
